title: Targeting GRB2 with Polyphyllin H overcomes PIKFYVE inhibitor resistance in bladder cancer by blocking Akt-SREBP1-SCD1 pathway.
authors: Song, Yu-Song; Liu, Chen-Kai; Jiang, Wu-Shuang; Liu, Jue; Liu, Yue-Xuan; Yu, Fei-Xue; Liu, Gao; Xu, Tian-Rui; Sang, Jun
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究GRB2抑制剂PPH与PIKFYVE抑制剂联用抗膀胱癌，涉及分子动力学模拟蛋白-配体互作，但核心是蛋白-小分子而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与TF-DNA课题关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Targeting PIKFYVE has emerged as a promising anticancer strategy; however, its efficacy is often limited by adaptive resistance. This study aimed to investigate the efficacy and resistance mechanisms of PIKFYVE inhibitors in bladder cancer, and discover a phytochemical capable of overcoming the adaptive resistance, thereby establishing a potent and safe combination therapy. METHODS: The anti-proliferative effects of PIKFYVE inhibitors and phytochemical polyphyllin H (PPH) were evaluated in a panel of cancer cell lines. Apoptosis was assessed by flow cytometry. Molecular mechanisms were investigated using integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses, complemented by functional validation using gene knockdown and pharmacological inhibition. The interaction between GRB2 and PPH was characterized by surface plasmon resonance, cellular thermal shift assays, and molecular dynamics simulations. Gene expression, correlation, and survival data were analyzed using public databases. Therapeutic synergy between PPH and PIKFYVE inhibitors was assessed both in vitro and in vivo. RESULTS: PIKFYVE inhibitors suppressed bladder cancer growth and overcame cisplatin resistance via autophagy blockade, but concurrently triggered a growth factor receptor binding protein 2 (GRB2)-dependent EGFR-Akt-SREBP lipogenic axis as a compensatory adaptive resistance mechanism. We identified PPH as a novel GRB2 inhibitor that binds specifically to the c-SH3/SH2 interface via a steric bottleneck involving key residues (Phe62, Ile65, Phe182). PPH suppressed the Akt-SREBP1-SCD1 cascade, inhibiting lipogenesis and tumor proliferation even under lipid-rich conditions. PPH disrupted this resistance mechanism, leading to strong synergistic antitumor activity without toxicity. CONCLUSION: Our findings reveal a GRB2-mediated adaptive resistance pathway centered on lipid reprogramming and establish PPH as a clinically translatable GRB2 inhibitor that synergizes with PIKFYVE-targeted therapy.
abstract_zh: 背景：靶向PIKFYVE已成为一种有前景的抗癌策略；然而，其疗效常受适应性耐药限制。本研究旨在探讨PIKFYVE抑制剂在膀胱癌中的疗效及耐药机制，并发现一种能够克服适应性耐药的植物化学物，从而建立一种强效且安全的联合治疗方案。方法：在一组癌细胞系中评估了PIKFYVE抑制剂和植物化学物重楼皂苷H（PPH）的抗增殖效果。通过流式细胞术评估细胞凋亡。利用整合转录组学和蛋白质组学分析研究分子机制，并通过基因敲低和药理学抑制进行功能验证。通过表面等离子体共振、细胞热位移实验和分子动力学模拟表征GRB2与PPH之间的相互作用。使用公共数据库分析基因表达、相关性和生存数据。在体外和体内评估PPH与PIKFYVE抑制剂之间的治疗协同作用。结果：PIKFYVE抑制剂通过自噬阻断抑制膀胱癌生长并克服顺铂耐药，但同时触发生长因子受体结合蛋白2（GRB2）依赖的EGFR-Akt-SREBP脂质生成轴，作为代偿性适应性耐药机制。我们鉴定PPH为一种新型GRB2抑制剂，通过涉及关键残基（Phe62、Ile65、Phe182）的空间瓶颈特异性结合c-SH3/SH2界面。PPH抑制Akt-SREBP1-SCD1级联，即使在脂质丰富条件下也能抑制脂质生成和肿瘤增殖。PPH破坏这一耐药机制，导致强效协同抗肿瘤活性且无毒性。结论：我们的发现揭示了一种以脂质重编程为中心的GRB2介导的适应性耐药通路，并将PPH确立为一种临床可转化的GRB2抑制剂，与PIKFYVE靶向治疗协同作用。
